subject.title: feat(codex): surface native questions and goals

question: Should OpenClaw force upstream Codex `features.goals` off for every thread, including threads whose configuration explicitly enables it, or default it off while preserving an explicit opt-in?
rationale: The forced override prevents unowned automatic continuation, but it also changes an upstream stable default and discards existing explicit configuration; source inspection cannot determine the intended compatibility policy.

options.title: Default off, honor opt-in
options.body: Keep safe OpenClaw defaults while allowing an explicit thread configuration to enable upstream goal tools and continuation with focused lifecycle tests.

options.title: Force goals off everywhere
options.body: Retain the unconditional override, but treat it as an intentional compatibility change with maintainer approval, documentation, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Split goal support
options.body: Land the structured-question work separately and defer native goal commands until OpenClaw has a settled run-owner and continuation policy.

recommendation.title: Default off, honor opt-in
recommendation.body: Keep safe OpenClaw defaults while allowing an explicit thread configuration to enable upstream goal tools and continuation with focused lifecycle tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The assignee also has the strongest recent merged history in the Codex app-server lifecycle and routing area.
